newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, look to a better economy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, look to a better economy.

text.p: Singapore's stock market on Friday shrugged off weak economic data to end the week on a firmer note on hopes of a better economic performance in 1997.
"We believe the economic condition is unlikely to deteriorate further as consensus is a recovery is likely by second quarter next year," a dealer with a European house said.
On Friday, Singapore reported a slowdown in all major sectors in the third quarter and said the economy had been badly hit by a global slowdown in the electronics industry.
After a flat open at 2,103.52, the key Straits Times Industrials Index ended at 2,117.23, up 14.50 points.
Market turnover was moderately active at 129.5 million shares with gainers beating losers by 218 to 104.
Some analysts said market valuations were becoming more attractive and encouraged "bottom-fishing" by investors.
Speculative and small capitalised stocks dominated trade. Malaysian Metroplex, which ended Singapore $0.03 up at S$1.70, topped the actives with 7.4 million shares.

Metro Holdings rose S$0.32 (US$0.23) to S$4.96 and Bukit Sembawang Estate shed S$0.40 to $32.40. Electronic counters were quiet, with the SES Electronics index flat at 81.47 ahead of the U.S. semiconductor data expected shortly.
